name: F5 Certified Technology Specialist, BIG-IP DNS

evaluation.rationale: Independent reviews of the stored evidence produced specialty: 3. The existing unordered-specialty rule applies when at least one reviewer identifies a specialty track. See each persona rationale for the supporting factors and limitations.

hiroshi-tanaka.rationale: The F5 administrator prerequisite and DNS-specific expertise fit a narrow technical extension rather than general progression; product dependence and multiple-choice testing limit broader network-defense claims.

maria-okonkwo.rationale: BIG-IP DNS knowledge builds on an administrator credential and serves a distinct network specialty. The proctored exam can screen platform familiarity, while multiple-choice assessment leaves practical DNS engineering unproven.

alex-novak.rationale: BIG-IP DNS is a narrow extension to prior F5 administration, matching the unordered specialty rubric. Three years of expected experience add context, but a multiple-choice exam cannot establish broader expert network defense.
